id: HL-03, HL-04, HL-05, HL-06 (0.1.2 handoff-lint, blocking rules re-judged)
note: Re-judged blocking rules, each pinned both ways (a former false refusal now passes, a true catch still blocks). HL-03 step1-mismatch: backticks, a `— proposed` mark (with or without a `(…)` note) and item 1 = Step 1 + ` — ` detail pass, and so does the same backticked command with only ` — ` detail after it on either side; an extra argument, a glued word, a dropped second command, a different edit after the same command, an empty Step 1 or a different wording still blocks. HL-04 id-range: a range of ids no chain file defines passes; a range hiding ids the stage ledger.md or the base's ledger pointer defines blocks until the draft names them alone; a range whose ends differ in kind, one that runs backwards or one over 1000 ids always blocks; a range on a pointer line naming inflight.md blocks; a range hiding ids the stage inflight.md table rows define blocks until the draft names them alone (the own previous file of a foreign base: HL-04-own-previous-ids) (a ledger pointer line naming ledger.md always blocks: the earlier D-2..D-3 lines). HL-05 recipe-placeholder: a `script: none` note, a printed value right after `=` or `-` in expected outputs and words inside an agent prompt pass; a whole-prompt placeholder (bare or quoted), a pointer inside a prompt or in expected outputs, a `--prompt=` flag's value, a placeholder before an agent prompt, a placeholder path, a bare stand-in in expected outputs and a pointer to a stated path block, class ask included. HL-06 recipe-script: an earlier handoff's copy blocks until `evidence --keep` names it in this run (dup, no second copy); the fix text says so, and after it this handoff's MANIFEST lists the earlier copy. Review round 3: an identical Step 1 and item 1 pass whatever they end in (a proposed mark with a note, `— done when`), the mark is stripped on both sides, runs of spaces do not count, and a backticked second command after ` — ` on either side blocks; a range that starts a ledger line or table row blocks, and so does one covering a Q- table row or an X- ledger line of the stage ledger, or ids the draft itself defines, while one of its ids is never named alone; words after a `prompt:` argument pass and a placeholder path inside a prompt blocks.
